# Luc Jodet

> Entrepreneur and investor — co-founder of Arianee, former partner at XAnge — now a PhD candidate at EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) researching AI and job displacement.

Luc Jodet has spent the last decade building and backing technology companies at the frontier of digital ownership. He began his career as a business analyst at a Fortune 500 company, then co-founded BUYECO (2014–2017), a Swiss renewable-energy marketplace, where he first encountered blockchain through energy-traceability solutions.

In 2017 he co-founded Arianee, the open protocol for digital product passports adopted by luxury houses such as Breitling, Lacoste, and Panerai. Arianee raised over $30 million. He went on to co-found NFT Factory (2022–2025), the Paris hub for the French web3 ecosystem, and joined XAnge (2022–2025), one of Europe's leading early-stage venture firms, as a partner focused on web3 and crypto.

He holds a Master's degree from Sciences Po and a Bachelor of Economics.

He is now a PhD candidate at EPFL, studying how artificial intelligence transforms labor markets — which tasks and occupations are displaced, which are created, and how firms, workers, and policymakers can navigate the transition.

## Key facts

- Full name: Luc Jodet
- Current: PhD candidate, EPFL, "AI and Job Displacement" (in progress)
- Co-founder, Arianee (2017–present)
- Co-founder, NFT Factory (2022–2025)
- Partner, XAnge (2022–2025)
- Co-founder, BUYECO (2014–2017)
- Education: Sciences Po (Master's), Bachelor of Economics
- Angel investments include Morpho, Bolero, and Rain.fi (acquired by Jupiter)
